columns.rationale: distinct_count is 3322, exactly matching dataset.row_count of 3322, with null_rate 0.0, so tailnum uniquely identifies each aircraft record.

Landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but all sample_values (1956.0, 1959.0, 1963.0, ...) are integral manufacture years between min 1956.0 and max 1973.0 shown, so cast to INTEGER; null_rate 0.021072 (70 nulls) means the value is retained as nullable.
null_rate is 0.0 and distinct_values are a closed set of 3 categories (Fixed wing multi engine, Fixed wing single engine, Rotorcraft), so kept as required text.
null_rate is 0.0 across 35 distinct manufacturer names (e.g. AIRBUS, BOEING, BELL), kept as required text.
null_rate is 0.0 with 127 distinct model codes such as 172E and 421C, kept as required text.
distinct_values are exactly 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 with null_rate 0.0, an integral count of engines, so cast DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER.
null_rate is 0.0 and all 48 distinct values from min 2.0 to max 450.0 sampled (2.0, 4.0, 5.0, ...) are integral seat counts, so cast to INTEGER.

null_rate is 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows null), an extremely sparse column, but the 13 distinct_values present (90.0 to 432.0) are integral so it is cast to INTEGER and retained nullable rather than dropped.
null_rate is 0.0 with a closed set of 6 distinct engine types (4 Cycle, Reciprocating, Turbo-fan, Turbo-jet, Turbo-prop, Turbo-shaft), kept as required text.
is_airbyte_metadata is true, a capture-tool identifier column, dropped per policy.
is_airbyte_metadata is true with a single distinct_value (2026-09-02T23:26:22) representing the capture timestamp, dropped per policy.
is_airbyte_metadata is true with the single distinct_value '{}', a capture-tool metadata payload, dropped per policy.

decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across dataset.row_count 3322, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is needed.
tailnum has distinct_count 3322 exactly equal to row_count 3322 with null_rate 0.0, so it plausibly identifies one row per aircraft and is declared the sole grain key.
year has null_rate 0.021072 (70 null_count), a low but nonzero rate, so nulls are retained rather than failing the build.
speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows null), making it sparsely populated; it is retained as nullable rather than dropped since the remaining 23 values carry information.
year, engines, seats, and speed all land as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sampled and distinct value shown (e.g. engines 1.0-4.0, seats 2.0-450.0) is integral, so all four are cast to INTEGER.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry only capture-tool bookkeeping values, so all three are dropped.

purpose: silver_nyc_planes is a cleaned registry of individual aircraft (tail numbers) used by NYC-area flight datasets, feeding downstream joins between flights and the physical aircraft that flew them.
usage: Join to flight-level fact tables on tailnum; treat year and speed as optionally null and filter or coalesce them before aggregation, since speed is populated for under 1% of rows and year is missing for about 2% of rows.
limitations: Pipeline metadata columns (_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, _airbyte_meta) were dropped and carry no business meaning; speed is retained despite a 99.3% null rate because no evidence supported dropping it, so most consumers should not rely on it without explicit null handling; no duplicate rows were found so no dedupe logic was needed.
